detail.calibrationDesc: Calibration is performed on the device itself. These guides walk you through each step.
detail.tiltCalibrationDesc: Corrects the tilt sensor. Menu: DOWN 4s → "inC" → FIRE → "YES CAL" → FIRE. 8 positions on a flat surface.
detail.compassCalibrationDesc: Aligns the compass sensor. Menu: DOWN 4s → "H_Ang" → FIRE → "HACAL" → FIRE → "YES CAL" → FIRE. Outdoors, 8 positions facing North.
detail.measurementModeDesc: Choose what value the device displays and returns when you take a measurement.
detail.remoteControlDesc: Trigger measurement remotely from the app without pressing the device button.

mode.hdDesc: Flat map distance to the target, ignoring elevation. Most common for surveying.
mode.vdDesc: Height difference between device and target. Positive = target is above, negative = below.
mode.sdDesc: Direct line-of-sight distance from device to target. The raw distance the laser measures.
mode.incDesc: Vertical angle to the target in degrees. 0° = level, positive = uphill, negative = downhill.
mode.htDesc: Measures height of an object by shooting its top and base. Requires two measurements.
mode.azDesc: Compass bearing to the target (0°–360°). North = 0°, East = 90°, South = 180°, West = 270°.
mode.mlDesc: Distance between two remote points. Shoot both points from the same position to calculate.

tilt.step1Detail:
On the device:
1. Press-and-hold DOWN 4 sec → "UnitS" appears
2. Press DOWN until "inC" appears
3. Press FIRE → "no CAL" appears
4. Press UP or DOWN → "YES CAL" appears
5. Press FIRE → "C1_Fd" appears (calibration starts)
tilt.step2Title: Place on a flat, level surface
tilt.step2Detail:
Put the TruPulse on a flat, stable surface (within 15° of level).
Lenses facing forward. Make sure buttons are accessible for each position.
tilt.step3Detail:
Lenses face forward (away from you).
Wait ~1 sec until steady, then press FIRE.
LCD shows "C2_Fd".
tilt.step4Detail:
Rotate 90° so lenses face DOWN.
Wait ~1 sec, press FIRE.
LCD shows "C3_Fd".
tilt.step5Title: C3: Lenses BACK → FIRE  /  C4: Lenses UP → FIRE
tilt.step5Detail:
C3: Rotate 90° → lenses face BACK (toward you).
⚠ 360R: Hang buttons over edge of surface.
Wait ~1 sec, press FIRE (short press!).

C4: Rotate 90° → lenses face UP.
Wait ~1 sec, press FIRE. LCD shows "C5_Fd".
tilt.step6Title: C5: Rotate along optical axis → Lenses FORWARD → FIRE
tilt.step6Detail:
Rotate 90° ALONG the optical axis (roll the device).
Lenses should face forward again, but the device is now rotated 90° from Position 1.
Wait ~1 sec, press FIRE. LCD shows "C6_Fd".
tilt.step7Title: C6–C8: DOWN → BACK → UP → FIRE each
tilt.step7Detail:
Same rotation as C2–C4, but in the rolled orientation:

C6: Rotate 90° → lenses DOWN → wait, FIRE.
C7: Rotate 90° → lenses BACK → wait, FIRE.
C8: Rotate 90° → lenses UP → FIRE.

Device calculates result.
tilt.step8Detail:
PASS → Press FIRE to save and return.

FAiL1: Excessive motion (not held steady)
FAiL2: Magnetic saturation
FAiL3: Mathematical fit error
FAiL4: Convergence error
FAiL6: Wrong orientations

On FAIL → press FIRE, repeat from C1.
Abort anytime: long-press UP or DOWN (previous calibration restored).

compass.step1Detail:
Compass calibration must be performed outdoors.
Stand away from vehicles, fences, buildings,
electronics, and any metal objects.

Face towards Magnetic North (±15°).
compass.step2Detail:
On the device:
1. Press-and-hold DOWN 4 sec → "UnitS" appears
2. Press DOWN until "H_Ang" appears
3. Press FIRE → "dECLn" appears
4. Press DOWN → "HACAL" appears
5. Press FIRE → "no CAL" appears
6. Press UP or DOWN → "YES CAL" appears
7. Press FIRE → "C1_Fd" appears (calibration starts)
compass.step3Title: C1: Facing North, lenses FORWARD → FIRE
compass.step3Detail:
Hold the device facing North, lenses forward.
Wait ~1 sec until steady, press FIRE.
LCD shows "C2_Fd".
compass.step4Detail:
Rotate 90° so lenses face DOWN.
Wait ~1 sec, press FIRE.
LCD shows "C3_Fd".
compass.step5Title: C3: Lenses BACK → FIRE  /  C4: Lenses UP → FIRE
compass.step5Detail:
C3: Rotate 90° → lenses face BACK (toward you).
Wait ~1 sec, press FIRE.

C4: Rotate 90° → lenses face UP.
Wait ~1 sec, press FIRE. LCD shows "C5_Fd".
compass.step6Title: C5: Rotate along optical axis → Lenses FORWARD → FIRE
compass.step6Detail:
Rotate 90° ALONG the optical axis (roll the device).
Lenses forward again, serial port pointing UP.
Wait ~1 sec, press FIRE. LCD shows "C6_Fd".
compass.step7Title: C6–C8: DOWN → BACK → UP → FIRE each
compass.step7Detail:
Same rotation as C2–C4, in the rolled orientation:

C6: Rotate 90° → lenses DOWN → wait, FIRE.
C7: Rotate 90° → lenses BACK → wait, FIRE.
C8: Rotate 90° → lenses UP → FIRE.

Device calculates result.
compass.step8Detail:
PASS → Press FIRE to save and return.

FAiL1: Excessive motion (not held steady)
FAiL2: Magnetic saturation (field too strong)
FAiL3: Mathematical fit error
FAiL4: Convergence error
FAiL6: Wrong orientations

On FAIL → press FIRE, repeat from C1.
If it fails repeatedly, do Tilt Cal first.
Abort anytime: long-press UP or DOWN (previous calibration restored).

text(map).view_move_b: Drag with a finger to move the map. Tap Next when you are ready.
text(map).view_zoom_b: Spread two fingers to zoom in, pinch to zoom out.
text(map).view_mode_b: This button switches between 2D (straight down) and tilted 3D.
text(map).view_north_b: Double-tap the same button to put north back up.
text(map).view_basemap_b: The background map is set in Settings. Open ≡ → Settings → Map & tiles.
text(map).view_relief_b: Tap "Add layer" and choose "国土地理院（赤色立体図）" (GSI red relief) to lay it over the current map. Ridges and valleys show as shades of red.
text(map).view_opacity_b: Move the slider of the red relief map to change how much shows through. Compare with the map below in the preview above.
text(map).view_backToMap_b: Tap ← at the top left to go back. The map now shows the layer you added.
text(map).data_folder_b: Kokage Map works on one folder at a time. The "Practice" folder is open now.
text(map).data_open_b: This button lists what is in the folder.
text(map).data_gpkg_b: The "Practice" heading holds the data (a GeoPackage, the file Practice.gpkg). QGIS opens it as is.
text(map).data_layers_b: It holds three layers: areas, routes and points. A layer is a set of data with the same shape.
text(map).data_hide_b: Tap the eye at the right of "Areas" to hide them from the map.
text(map).data_hiddenClose_b: Close the list and look at the map. The hidden areas are not shown.
text(map).data_hiddenOpen_b: Open the list to bring the areas back.
text(map).data_show_b: Tap the eye again to bring them back.
text(map).data_zoomTo_b: Double-tap the "Areas" row to move the map to where the areas are.
text(map).data_select_b: This button lets you pick things on the map.
text(map).data_pick_b: Tap an area on the map to see its name and memo.
text(map).data_table_b: This button lists the selected layer as a table.
text(map).record_open_b: Choose which layer to write to.
text(map).record_pick_b: Tap the "Points" row. New features go into the selected layer.
text(map).record_pen_b: With the pen you write into the selected layer.
text(map).record_place_b: Tap anywhere on the map to place a point there.
text(map).record_select_b: Switch to the select tool and tap the point. Its details appear below.
text(map).record_name_b: Type a name in the "name" field.
text(map).record_route_b: Open the layer list and tap the "Routes" row.
text(map).record_draw_b: Close the list, take the pen and tap a few places on the map. ↶ removes the last point. ✓ at the bottom right saves it.
text(map).record_area_b: Open the layer list again and tap the "Areas" row.
text(map).photo_open_b: Photos are imported into the open folder.
text(map).photo_legend_b: Faded photos with a mark have no location. They cannot be placed on the map, so turn on location in your camera settings.
text(map).photo_import_b: Tap a photo to import just that one. Long-press to choose several.
text(map).photo_done_b: Imported photos are copied into the practice folder and shown where they were taken. Tapping its marker with the select tool opens it too.
text(map).gps_tool_b: This button switches to the GPS tool. The points layer is selected for you.
text(map).gps_record_b: Tap to record a point where you are. Hold to keep measuring while pressed. Indoors there may be no fix.
text(map).yours_folder_t: Your everyday map and other folders
text(map).yours_folder_b: "Open my map" on Home opens your everyday map (Documents/KokageMap). Points and lines go into "マイ地図". To open just one folder inside it, use "Choose a folder to open".
text(map).yours_drive_b: A folder synced with Drive shows the same data on your other devices. Scan the code from "Share by QR" in the menu you get by long-pressing the folder with a phone camera and it lands in "共有" in the other person's everyday map. Start syncing from Settings → Drive sync.
text(map).yours_qgis_b: Open KokageMap.qgs in your everyday map (or the .qgs in another folder) with QGIS to see it as the app shows it. Colors changed in QGIS come back to the app.
text(map).style_open_b: The look is changed from the layer list.
text(map).style_color_b: Tap "Polygon" to open it, scroll down a little and tap the "Fill color" swatch. Pick any color.
text(map).style_backToMap_b: Tap ← at the top left to go back to the map.
text(map).style_look_b: Close the list. The areas now have the new color.
text(map).style_addView_b: A layer can have several looks. Open the list and long-press "Areas" and choose "Add view". A "New view" is added at the top.
text(map).style_viewMenu_b: Long-press the "New view" row and choose "Style".
text(map).style_viewColor_b: Choose a different fill color. Only what you change is stored in this View.
text(map).style_viewBack_b: Tap ← to go back to the map.
text(map).style_viewLook_b: Close the list. The areas now use the new View's color. The View on top wins.
text(map).style_viewHide_b: Open the list and tap the eye at the right of "New view" to turn it off. Each tap switches.
text(map).style_close_b: Close the list. The areas are back to the "Areas" color. With a filter, a View can change only some features.
text(map).record_edit_b: Tap "Edit" in the details. The panel turns into the editor.
text(map).record_attrs_b: Tap "Attributes" at the top right. The panel rises to the top.
text(map).record_save_b: Tap "Save" to write it and return to the details. Nothing is written until you save.
text(map).record_drawArea_b: Tap a few places like the line and tap ✓. The last point joins the first to make an area.
text(map).fix_select_b: Pick the feature you want to fix.
text(map).fix_pick_b: Tap an area on the map.
text(map).fix_edit_b: Tap "Edit". The map locks to top-down and the left side turns into edit tools.
text(map).fix_drag_b: Drag a white circle (vertex). Tap a small dot midway along an edge to add one. Move the map with two fingers.
text(map).fix_undo_b: ↶ on the left undoes one step at a time.
text(map).fix_again_b: Shape it as you like. There are also move, rotate and scale tools.
text(map).fix_save_b: "Save" writes it. To stop, use "Cancel" or ← at the top left.
text(map).fix_delete_b: Long-press "Delete" under the details. It is a long press so you do not delete by accident.
text(map).photo_pick_b: Tap the new photo row in the list. The map moves to where it was taken and the photo is selected. Tapping its camera mark on the map works too.
text(map).photo_view_b: Tap the zoom button at the top right of the panel to view it large.

onboarding.welcomeDesc:
A GeoPackage-based geographic information management app.
Let's set up the required permissions to get started.
onboarding.storageDisclosure: Kokage Map requires full storage access to read and write GeoPackage files, save map cache, and manage project data.
onboarding.storageRequired: Basic app features are unavailable without this permission
onboarding.locationDisclosure:
Kokage Map collects location data to display your current position on the map, perform GPS surveys, record GPS tracks, and share your live location with party members.

Location data is stored on your device. Your live location is shared with room members only while you are in a location-sharing party.
onboarding.locationDeniedNote: GPS features will be unavailable. You can enable it later in Settings.
onboarding.bluetoothDisclosure:
Bluetooth permission is required to connect external GNSS devices (RTK receivers) and laser rangefinders.
You can skip this if you don't use external devices.
